plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of two nested surfaces over a labeled coordinate frame, with the x axis coming forward to the lower left, the y axis running right, and the z axis vertical. The outer surface is a downward-opening paraboloid drawn as a translucent shell shaded in blue and salmon; its apex sits on the z axis at the marked point (0, 0, 2), and it widens as it descends, closing in a broad elliptical rim near the xy-plane. Nested inside is a cone with its vertex at the origin, opening upward and shaded darker blue-gray, its circular top rim appearing as an ellipse partway up the paraboloid's interior. Two horizontal arrows carry the equations: the left arrow points to the inner cone and reads z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), the right arrow points to the outer shell and reads z = 2 - x^2 - y^2. Dashed segments trace the hidden part of the z axis and the far side of the base rim. Nesting one surface inside the other makes the enclosed solid legible, with a curved dome above and a pointed conical floor below. The sketch fixes the region whose volume is to be set up as a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates.

elements: translucent downward-opening paraboloid shell z = 2 - x^2 - y^2, apex at (0,0,2), base rim circle of radius sqrt(2) in the xy-plane
opaque cone z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2) with vertex at origin, opening upward, top rim circle of radius 1 at height z = 1 where the surfaces intersect
z-axis vertical through the origin with arrowhead, dashed hidden segment inside the surfaces
y-axis pointing right with arrowhead
x-axis pointing forward/lower-left with arrowhead
point label (0, 0, 2) at the paraboloid apex
left arrow annotation pointing to the cone with equation label
right arrow annotation pointing to the paraboloid with equation label
dashed hidden back edge of the paraboloid base rim
radial ray from the z-axis outward at height 0 showing coordinate r
vertical segment at radius r spanning from the cone surface (z = r) to the paraboloid surface (z = 2 - r^2)
thin ring marker at the intersection circle (r = 1, z = 1) where cone meets paraboloid

interactions.label: r
interactions.teaches: Sweeping r from the z-axis outward moves the vertical segment between the cone (z = r) and the paraboloid (z = 2 - r^2); the segment shrinks to zero at r = 1, showing exactly why the solid's vertical bounds run from the cone up to the paraboloid and why r ranges over [0, 1]

interactions.label: Equation labels
interactions.teaches: Switching labels from z = sqrt(x^2+y^2) and z = 2 - x^2 - y^2 to the cylindrical forms z = r and z = 2 - r^2 reveals that both surfaces depend only on the radius — a circular sweep highlight around the z-axis makes the radial symmetry that motivates cylindrical coordinates visible
Rotating the scene lets the learner see the cone nested inside the paraboloid and verify that the enclosed solid has a conical floor and a dome-shaped ceiling

demo_steps.title: A radial segment near the axis
demo_steps.narration: At r = 0.3 the vertical segment runs from the cone surface at z = r = 0.3 up to the paraboloid at z = 2 - r^2 = 1.91 — one thin column of the solid whose volume we will integrate.

demo_steps.title: Approach the intersection
demo_steps.narration: Increase r toward 1: the segment gets shorter as the two surfaces converge. At r = 1 the segment vanishes because z = r and z = 2 - r^2 coincide — the surfaces meet on the circle r = 1, z = 1, giving the outer limit of the radial integral.

demo_steps.title: Why cylindrical?
demo_steps.narration: Switch to cylindrical labels: the equations become z = r and z = 2 - r^2 with no angular dependence at all. The highlighted circular symmetry shows the whole solid is described by 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, 0 ≤ r ≤ 1, r ≤ z ≤ 2 - r^2.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: paraboloid z = 2 - r^2 for 0 ≤ r ≤ sqrt(2) ≈ 1.414 (apex at z = 2, base rim in z = 0 plane); cone z = r for 0 ≤ r ≤ 1 (vertex at origin, top rim at z = 1). Surfaces intersect exactly on the circle r = 1, z = 1. Axes: +z up, +y to screen right, +x coming forward toward lower-left (classic three-axis pose); axis arrows extend ~2.5 units. Paraboloid rendered translucent (double-sided, opacity ~0.35) with a blue-to-salmon gradient shading — cool blue #7fa8d9 on the upper/right, salmon #e8a48c on the lower/left as in the source; cone more opaque blue-gray #6a7f9a. Vertical segment is a bright orange #ff8800 rod from (r, z=r) to (r, z=2-r^2) placed along the +y direction so it faces the viewer, with a thin radial line on the xy-plane from the axis to its foot labeled r. Intersection ring at r = 1, z = 1 as a thin bright circle. Dashed grey for the hidden z-axis segment (z from 0 to ~2 inside the shell) and the back half of the base rim ellipse. In Cylindrical mode the equation labels read 'z = r' (cone) and 'z = 2 - r^2' (paraboloid) and a semi-transparent golden annular sweep rotates once around the z-axis to signal radial symmetry.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the paraboloid and cone as parametric surface geometries (radial segments ~64, height segments ~32) so silhouettes stay smooth under orbit. Backface rendering with lower opacity helps sell the translucency. The vertical segment and radial foot line update reactively from the slider; clamp the segment's lower/upper endpoints with the exact formulas z = r and z = 2 - r^2 so the learner sees it collapse at r = 1. Keep both label sprites in the scene and cross-fade text on the toggle rather than recreating geometry; the golden symmetry sweep can be a torus/cylinder shader that fades in only in Cylindrical mode. Labels (0,0,2), axis letters, and equation arrows should be camera-facing sprites so they stay legible while orbiting.

authoredContext:
Let E be the region bounded below by the cone z=x2+y2 and above by the paraboloid z=2−x2−y2. (the figure). Set up a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates to find the volume of the region, using the following orders of integration:

Setting up a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates over a conical region.

A paraboloid with equation z = 2 minus x squared minus y squared opening down, and within it, a cone with equation z = the square root of (x squared + y squared) pointing down.

discrepancies: A large bright red-orange torus (intersection ring at z=1) dominates the figure and does not appear in the source
An orange rod and radial 'r' foot line are added elements not present in the source
The salmon-to-blue pastel gradient of the source surfaces reads as muted gray/beige in the render, so the warm left/cool right color contrast is largely lost
The cone in the source is semi-transparent showing the dashed z-axis through it; the generated cone is nearly opaque dark blue-gray
The intersection region/ellipse shown in the source (where cone meets paraboloid interior) is obscured by the added torus and rod
evaluation.notes: Core surfaces, axes, dashed z-axis, and equation labels are correct and the slider/steps/coordinate-toggle interactions are excellent, but the added glowing red ring and orange rod clutter the figure and the signature salmon-to-blue surface coloring is lost, weakening resemblance to the source.
action_items: Make the intersection ring thin and subtle (or toggleable) so it doesn't dominate the default view, and tone down/remove the always-on orange rod
Increase surface saturation/contrast so the salmon-to-blue gradient reads clearly as in the source, and make the cone translucent enough to reveal the dashed z-axis
Set a clearer default camera framing matching the source's three-quarter view with the cone visible inside the dome

feedback.rationale: The plan correctly captured the concept (concept_accuracy 5, empty plan_action_items), but the generator hallucinated extra elements (torus, rod) and executed colors/translucency/camera wrongly — all concrete implementation fixes, not conceptual ones.

discrepancies: Composition/orientation differs noticeably: in the source the paraboloid is a wide, squat dome viewed with y to the right and x coming forward-left, but the rendered figure shows a tall, narrow, edge-on shell that is much harder to recognize as the same solid
The cone z = sqrt(x^2+y^2) is barely visible in the render; in the source it is a clearly visible interior surface meeting the paraboloid at the rim circle
The dashed z-axis running from the origin up through (0,0,2) is prominent in the source but not apparent in the render
Source has no orange rod, radial foot line, or r marker dots; these are extra (pedagogically useful but not in the figure)
The base rim ellipse at z=0 (front solid/back dashed) in the source is not clearly reproduced in the render
evaluation.notes: The two surfaces, gradient coloring, and equation labels are correct and the interactions (r slider, Cartesian/Cylindrical toggle, intersection ring, step-through) are excellent, but the edge-on narrow composition makes the dome-and-cone solid hard to recognize and hides the cone and dashed axis.
action_items: Adjust the camera azimuth/elevation so the paraboloid reads as a wide squat dome (matching the source's vantage with y to the right and x forward-left) instead of an edge-on shell
Make the cone visually distinct from the paraboloid (stronger color contrast or slightly higher opacity) so the interior cone is clearly visible as in the source
Ensure the dashed z-axis segment from origin to (0,0,2) renders visibly through the translucent surfaces
Draw the base rim ellipse at z=0 with solid front and dashed back half as in the source

feedback.rationale: Concept accuracy and interactivity are perfect (5/5) with an empty plan action list — all issues (wrong camera angle, hidden cone, invisible dashed axis, missing base rim) are execution-level rendering fixes for the generator.

interactions.label: r
interactions.teaches: Sweeping r from the z-axis outward moves the vertical segment between the cone (z = r) and the paraboloid (z = 2 - r^2); the segment shrinks to zero at r = 1, showing exactly why the solid's vertical bounds run from the cone up to the paraboloid and why r ranges over [0, 1]

interactions.label: Equation labels
interactions.teaches: Switching labels from z = sqrt(x^2+y^2) and z = 2 - x^2 - y^2 to the cylindrical forms z = r and z = 2 - r^2 reveals that both surfaces depend only on the radius — a circular sweep highlight around the z-axis makes the radial symmetry that motivates cylindrical coordinates visible

demo_steps.title: A radial segment near the axis
demo_steps.narration: At r = 0.3 the vertical segment runs from the cone surface at z = r = 0.3 up to the paraboloid at z = 2 - r^2 = 1.91 — one thin column of the solid whose volume we will integrate.

demo_steps.title: Approach the intersection
demo_steps.narration: Increase r toward 1: the segment gets shorter as the two surfaces converge. At r = 1 the segment vanishes because z = r and z = 2 - r^2 coincide — the surfaces meet on the circle r = 1, z = 1, giving the outer limit of the radial integral.

demo_steps.title: Why cylindrical?
demo_steps.narration: Switch to cylindrical labels: the equations become z = r and z = 2 - r^2 with no angular dependence at all. The highlighted circular symmetry shows the whole solid is described by 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, 0 ≤ r ≤ 1, r ≤ z ≤ 2 - r^2.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: paraboloid z = 2 - r^2 for 0 ≤ r ≤ sqrt(2) ≈ 1.414 (apex at z = 2, base rim in z = 0 plane); cone z = r for 0 ≤ r ≤ 1 (vertex at origin, top rim at z = 1). Surfaces intersect exactly on the circle r = 1, z = 1. Axes: +z up, +y to screen right, +x coming forward toward lower-left (classic three-axis pose); axis arrows extend ~2.5 units. Paraboloid rendered translucent (double-sided, opacity ~0.35) with a blue-to-salmon gradient shading — cool blue #7fa8d9 on the upper/right, salmon #e8a48c on the lower/left as in the source; cone more opaque blue-gray #6a7f9a. Vertical segment is a bright orange #ff8800 rod from (r, z=r) to (r, z=2-r^2) placed along the +y direction so it faces the viewer, with a thin radial line on the xy-plane from the axis to its foot labeled r. Intersection ring at r = 1, z = 1 as a thin bright circle. Dashed grey for the hidden z-axis segment (z from 0 to ~2 inside the shell) and the back half of the base rim ellipse. In Cylindrical mode the equation labels read 'z = r' (cone) and 'z = 2 - r^2' (paraboloid) and a semi-transparent golden annular sweep rotates once around the z-axis to signal radial symmetry.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the paraboloid and cone as parametric surface geometries (radial segments ~64, height segments ~32) so silhouettes stay smooth under orbit. Backface rendering with lower opacity helps sell the translucency. The vertical segment and radial foot line update reactively from the slider; clamp the segment's lower/upper endpoints with the exact formulas z = r and z = 2 - r^2 so the learner sees it collapse at r = 1. Keep both label sprites in the scene and cross-fade text on the toggle rather than recreating geometry; the golden symmetry sweep can be a torus/cylinder shader that fades in only in Cylindrical mode. Labels (0,0,2), axis letters, and equation arrows should be camera-facing sprites so they stay legible while orbiting.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of two nested surfaces over a labeled coordinate frame, with the x axis coming forward to the lower left, the y axis running right, and the z axis vertical. The outer surface is a downward-opening paraboloid drawn as a translucent shell shaded in blue and salmon; its apex sits on the z axis at the marked point (0, 0, 2), and it widens as it descends, closing in a broad elliptical rim near the xy-plane. Nested inside is a cone with its vertex at the origin, opening upward and shaded darker blue-gray, its circular top rim appearing as an ellipse partway up the paraboloid's interior. Two horizontal arrows carry the equations: the left arrow points to the inner cone and reads z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), the right arrow points to the outer shell and reads z = 2 - x^2 - y^2. Dashed segments trace the hidden part of the z axis and the far side of the base rim. Nesting one surface inside the other makes the enclosed solid legible, with a curved dome above and a pointed conical floor below. The sketch fixes the region whose volume is to be set up as a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for radial coordinate r: the learner increases r from the z-axis outward, the vertical segment between z=r and z=2-r^2 updates until the surfaces meet, showing why cylindrical bounds run from the cone to the paraboloid.
- Toggle between Cartesian equations and cylindrical forms: the learner switches labels from z=sqrt(x^2+y^2) and z=2-x^2-y^2 to z=r and z=2-r^2, and the radial symmetry highlights, clarifying why cylindrical coordinates simplify the setup.

discrepancies: The cone in the source is a smooth reddish interior surface visible through the dome; in the render it appears as a dark slate-blue opaque band across the middle, making the interior look like a filled slab rather than a hollow cone surface.
An orange vertical rod, foot line, and 'r' label are added that do not exist in the source figure (pedagogically sensible, but not in the original).
The paraboloid dome looks somewhat squat/narrow compared with the source's broader dome, and its salmon-to-blue gradient is subtler than the source's warm left / cool right shading.
The 'z = 2 − x² − y²' label with its arrow sits right next to the y-axis tip, visually colliding with the axis annotation rather than clearly floating to the right as in the source.
evaluation.notes: Recognizable dome-over-cone figure with correct equations, axes, and excellent slider/step interactions, but the cone renders as a dark band, the dome proportions are squatter than the source, and the added rod/ring/sweep elements go beyond the original figure.
action_items: Lighten the cone material and reduce its opacity so it reads as a translucent reddish interior surface matching the source, not a dark band.
Reposition the 'z = 2 − x² − y²' label and its arrow further right and down, away from the y-axis arrow tip.
Widen/round the paraboloid profile slightly and strengthen the warm-to-cool color contrast to better match the source shading.
